method.one_call: Independent sessions with one cold synchronous ORT run; startup effects prevent a general speed claim from these single measurements.
method.warm: One session, one cold warmup and three measured synchronous ORT run_with_iobinding calls. Same explicit inputs each time; final state is not fed back. Hashing, snapshots, output validation and CPU references are outside the timer.
method.numerical_reference: Stable FP64 recurrence and separately BF16-rounded-each-step recurrence; relative RMSE is an error measure, not an acceptance bound or task-quality score.

limitations: FLOAT sequence accumulation matches adaptive Concat outputs bitwise in all four measured fixtures. This does not make native batched arithmetic equivalent to token_loop arithmetic.
Captured layer14 state relative RMSE versus FP64 is approximately 4.841% for adaptive batching and 1.449% for token_loop; attention is approximately 2.896% versus 0.643%.
Isolated warm operator ratios do not predict full-model throughput or general model quality.
Native operator provider DLL hashes and full-model runtime DLL hashes are independently recorded; these are distinct execution paths.
